title: Scaling sanity check & budget reset
summary: Quarterly check-in focused on unexpected traffic patterns during the fall promo, cost overrun mitigation, and a plan to balance latency targets with a temporary right-sizing of dedicated capacity. Agreement to run a 2-week stress benchmark and provide an updated pricing scenario and burst plan.
topics: Recent traffic surge and root-cause hypothesis
Dedicated vs hosted routing for peak promos
Next steps: benchmark, updated pricing, pilot plan

Miguel Alvarez: Provide recent request distribution and peak traces for Aug–Sep (due 2026-10-04)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-01
- Time: 15:00 PT (68 minutes)
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Laura (BlueOak Head of ML), Miguel (Platform), Anika (Finance)

Summary:
Jordan: quick qbr style checkpoint today to focus on the promo spike and the cost noise. we'll walk through what happened, then options.

Topics covered: cost, reliability, routing, burst/dedicated, security.

00:00:03 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Laura, Miguel, Anika — thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 Laura (BlueOak): Hi all, Laura here. Sorry ran over from the ops standup.
00:00:15 Miguel (BlueOak): Miguel — platform team.
00:00:18 Anika (BlueOak): Anika from finance. Morning.
00:00:22 Priya (Redwood): Priya here, SE. I'll own the benchmark and technical bits.
00:00:28 Jordan (Redwood): Awesome. Quick agenda: 1) what happened during the September promo, 2) cost breakdown, 3) short-term mitigation, 4) plan for reserved vs hosted, 5) next steps. Sound good?

00:01:02 Laura: yep. To start — big thanks, you saw the alerts. We had an unexpected 3x spike in gen requests during the midnight PST window when the promo emails dropped. Latency increased and cost spiked, finance freaked out a little.
00:01:18 Jordan: Understood. Miguel, do you have the traces or is it just aggregate?
00:01:24 Miguel: We pulled traces — I'll share them after. Quick note: requests had a long tail, a lot of retries from mobile clients that timed out then retried. Also some heavier contexts — longer prompt lengths for personalization.
00:01:40 Priya: That matches the token profile we saw in the dashboard — average seq length jumped from 128 to ~420 on those windows. That changes batching dynamics and KV cache hit rates.
00:01:52 Laura: Right, and we had some confusion about which environment was routing to Dedicated vs Hosted. A portion of requests fell back to hosted which increased variable cost.
00:02:05 Jordan: Got it. So two levers: routing policy correctness and capacity sizing. Quick question to finance — Anika, did the extra bill get flagged as an overrun on the monthly card or was it under your committed plan?
00:02:18 Anika: No committed shortfall, since we didn't reserve extra. The overrun hit variable usage and our month-to-date is 28% over forecast for the inference line-item. Not catastrophic but it's a red flag.
00:02:30 Jordan: Thanks. On the technical side, Priya, what's likely the main driver of latency increase?
00:02:36 Priya: Two things — longer sequences + more KV cache cold starts because we saw a lot of different user prefixes. That increases per-token compute and reduces batching efficiency. Also, retries lead to bursty short-window spikes — the runtime is optimized for steady throughput, bursts are more expensive.
00:02:55 Miguel: And just to add, our mobile SDK had a bug that retried too aggressively; we've patched it but the promo window already hit.

00:03:08 Jordan: Ok. For mitigation options: 1) short term: enable prefix caching and adjust routing so promo traffic pins to Dedicated pool with burst policy; 2) medium: run a stress benchmark and right-size dedicated capacity + prewarm cache; 3) longer: quantization profile on some models and prompt engineering to reduce seq lengths.
00:03:30 Laura: We want to avoid model quality regressions — the personalization is core to conversions. Quantization sounds risky.
00:03:36 Priya: Totally — quantization can be tuned. We can run a P0 pilot on a copy of the model and run A/B quality evals on the same prompt set. No production change without passing the eval.
00:03:47 Anika: From finance — short term we can approve a modest reserved commit for Oct if the numbers make sense. We need concrete delta vs current burn.
00:03:57 Jordan: We'll prepare two pricing scenarios: conservative (minimal reserved, rely on burst capacity) and optimized (larger reserved commit with lower unit cost). I'll include a forecast model.

00:04:10 Miguel: About routing, is it possible to do a canary so only a percent of promo traffic uses Dedicated initially? We want fallback in case Dedicated saturates.
00:04:18 Priya: Yes — Redwood supports percentage-based routing and automatic fallback to hosted-compatible variants when capacity is constrained. We can set latency SLOs and a fallback policy. There was some confusion in your config which led to unintended fallback; we'll help audit that.

00:04:40 Laura: Perfect. Security check — we need to confirm that audit logs and KMS usage didn't change with the fallback. We have a PCI-ish workflow.
00:04:49 Jordan: On audit logs and KMS: Dedicated still uses your KMS if configured and audit logs are preserved. We'll send the SOC2 / logs export process doc.
00:04:58 Anika: Please include retention durations — our compliance team needs 7 years for certain logs.
00:05:05 Jordan: Noted — we'll include the retention section.

00:05:18 Priya: For the benchmark, we'll need: 1) the exact request distribution (Miguel to share), 2) representative prompt sets (Laura), 3) desired SLOs (latency P95 target), and 4) whether you want a canary routing plan during the next promo. We'll run both steady-state and burst simulations.
00:05:40 Miguel: I'll export the Aug–Sep traces and a sample of the promo window. Expect that by tomorrow.
00:05:45 Laura: I'll send the personalization prompt set and conversion-weighted examples.

00:05:52 Jordan: Great — timeline idea: Priya runs benchmark starting next Monday for two weeks, Jordan sends updated pricing by Tuesday, BlueOak reviews and we meet back in two weeks to decide on reserved commit. Sound doable?
00:06:05 Anika: Works for finance; need decision by Oct 15 at latest to adjust procurement.
00:06:10 Jordan: We'll aim for that.

00:06:14 [15:00–15:15] Side note — quick walk-through of the cost breakout in the console. Jordan: here you can see token-level breakdown and which routes are falling back. Miguel: yep i see the sudden spike column.

00:06:58 Laura: A question on model variants — can we route to a compatible lighter variant for non-personalized flows (e.g., help center responses), and keep the heavy model for personalization?
00:07:08 Priya: Absolutely. You can set route-level model policies. For heavy personalization keep the higher quality model, for generic responses route to a cheaper variant. That alone can reduce unit cost significantly.
00:07:20 Miguel: Any gotchas around embeddings and reranking? We use embeddings for personalization features too — will that be affected by routing decisions?
00:07:29 Priya: Embeddings are a separate call type; you can colocate embedding workloads on separate pools or pin them to lower-cost variants. We'll recommend a layout based on your traffic patterns.

00:07:45 Anika: Ok, finance question — show me the numbers that justify reserved vs burst. We can't commit to a high reserve without seeing payback in 3 months.
00:07:56 Jordan: Understood — we'll include a 3-month payback scenario plus a sensitivity analysis for different promo frequencies.

00:08:04 Miguel: One more technical — during the spike we noticed an increase in 429s from the client side. Is that on Redwood rate limits or our SDK retry behavior?
00:08:14 Priya: Likely both interplay. The runtime has per-route throttles to protect capacity. If SDK retries immediately that makes pressure worse. We'll look at recommended retry backoff and client-side rate limiting.

00:08:30 Laura: Good. Also, can we get a short ops runbook for promo windows? Like prewarm cache, temporary routing rule, and rollback steps?
00:08:40 Jordan: Yes, we'll provide a one-page promo ops checklist and a suggested prewarm script.

00:08:49 [20:09] Jordan: Ok let's capture decisions: run 2-week benchmark; we try a small reserved commit if benchmark supports it; audit routing config; provide pricing scenarios; deliver ops runbook and retention/SOC2 docs.

00:09:05 Action confirmations: Miguel will send traces; Laura will send prompts; Anika will confirm decision timeline. Priya will schedule benchmark; Jordan will send pricing.

00:09:20 Laura: quick thought — if the benchmark shows lower-than-expected improvement from dedicated, what's the fallback?
00:09:28 Priya: If dedicated doesn't reduce unit cost enough we'll focus on prompt engineering + model variant split + small reserved commit only for critical routes. We'll also consider cache-friendly request shaping.

00:09:45 Anika: can you include a simplified one-slide ROI for finance to present to procurement?
00:09:52 Jordan: Yes, we'll add that to the pricing packet.

00:10:00 [wrap-up]
00:10:02 Jordan: Thanks all. We'll send the pricing sheet and the security docs today. Priya will kick off the benchmark and send calendar invites. Follow-up in two weeks.
00:10:15 Miguel: Thanks both.
00:10:18 Laura: Thanks.
00:10:20 Anika: Bye.

Notes and links referenced:
